bounded_slice.tested_scope: Static exact-commit reproduction of argus_skill/core/usage.py::ensure_project_events_standardized, its legacy history enumeration helper, and the direct AgentCliBackend._agent_io_log_path production call/path-selection boundary at Argus commit 2894b434affaff3a28c1fbbcd5c39f2e7a832236. This proves the helper/API-level post-marker gap but does not claim whole-program reachability of every context transition, repository-wide reference exhaustiveness, runtime contention behavior, Windows behavior, or no-fourth-writer exhaustiveness.
observations: ensure_project_events_standardized returns immediately whenever events.migration-v2.json exists, both before entering and again after acquiring events.migration-v2.lock.

Before acquiring the migration lock it snapshots legacy source paths from <project_root>/.argus/events.jsonl using _event_history_paths; that helper includes numeric generations in oldest-to-newest order followed by the live file.

The migration appends directly to <project_root>/events.jsonl while holding events.migration-v2.lock, fsyncs best-effort, then atomically writes a version-2 marker containing source_files and row counts but no source signature/version that would invalidate the marker if a legacy source later changes.

AgentCliBackend._agent_io_log_path calls ensure_project_events_standardized and selects <project_root>/events.jsonl only when a project usage context is present. With no project context, an explicit ARGUS_SKILL_AGENT_IO_LOG path wins; otherwise options.working_dir selects <working_dir>/.argus/events.jsonl. The legacy branch does not consult the migration marker.

Therefore the exact helper/API composition admits this bounded counterexample: migrate legacy rows and create the marker; later invoke AgentIO logging without project usage context but with working_dir equal to that project root, which selects .argus/events.jsonl; then invoke a project-context path again. ensure_project_events_standardized sees the existing marker and returns 0, so the later legacy append is not migrated by this protocol.

This is sufficient to reject marker-existence alone as a complete source-change seal at the tested helper/API boundary. Whole-program proof that the no-project-context to project-context sequence is reachable in a deployed production flow remains open and is not inferred here.
bounded_slice.acceptance_effect: The candidate remains unresolved: an event-authority patch that only serializes the migration append cannot by itself guarantee completeness if legacy source writes remain possible after the one-shot marker. Either prove the legacy writer unreachable once the marker may exist, or make migration replay/source-change detection robust to later legacy writes.
